id:core.Actor rocs:status "active"^^xsd:string .
id:core.Actor rocs:example "Human maintainer or bot acting in GitLab"@und .

id:core.Actor rocs:guidanceMarkdown "# Actor (core.Actor)

## Definition
Ein handelndes Subjekt im System (Mensch oder System).

## Typical usage
- Used as the supertype for entities that can take actions and hold responsibilities.

## Common confusions
- Confused with passive artifacts (documents, datasets).
"@und .

id:core.Agent rocs:guidanceMarkdown "# Agent (core.Agent)

## Definition
Ein autonom/teilautonom handelnder Software-Akteur (LLM-Agent, Bot).

## Typical usage
- Used to model autonomous actors that take actions (e.g. triage, checks, proposals).

## Common confusions
- Confused with `core.Service` (a deployed runtime without decision-making autonomy).
"@und .

- Used to justify new IDs, deprecations, and relation additions.

## Common confusions
- Confused with a proposal; decisions are outcomes.

id:core.rel.conflicts_with rdf:type rocs:Relation .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rdfs:label "conflicts_with"@und .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with skos:definition "X steht im Konflikt/Widerspruch zu Y"@und .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:status "active"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:relationGroup "opposition"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:transitive false .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:symmetric true .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rdf:type owl:SymmetricProperty .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with owl:inverseOf id:core.rel.conflicts_with .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:axisDefault "left"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:example "core.Policy conflicts_with core.Policy (two rules cannot both hold for the same scope)"@und .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:antiExample "Using conflicts_with to express similarity (use `similar_to`)"@und .
id:core.rel.conflicts_with rocs:guidanceMarkdown "## Definition
`X conflicts_with Y` means X and Y cannot both be satisfied/true in the same scope (a direct contradiction or incompatibility).

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- Two statements/constraints cannot both be satisfied in the same scope.

## Do not use when
- You mean tradeoff/choice history (track in decisions) or simple difference without contradiction.

## Domain / Range
- Domain: policies/constraints/invariants
- Range: policies/constraints/invariants
"@und .
id:core.rel.depends_on rdf:type rocs:Relation .
id:core.rel.depends_on rdfs:label "depends_on"@und .
id:core.rel.depends_on skos:definition "X benötigt Y, um korrekt zu funktionieren"@und .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:status "active"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:relationGroup "dependency"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:transitive false .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:symmetric false .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:axisDefault "parents"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:example "core.Service depends_on core.IntegrationEdge (service needs an external integration)"@und .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:antiExample "Using depends_on for mere 'uses' relationships"@und .
id:core.rel.depends_on rocs:guidanceMarkdown "## Definition
`X depends_on Y` means X requires Y to function correctly (runtime/build/operational requirement).

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- X requires Y to function correctly (runtime, build, or operational requirement).

## Do not use when
- X just uses Y optionally or incidentally (use `uses`), or X is a part of Y (use `part_of`).

## Domain / Range
- Domain: any system element (`core.Service`, `core.Pipeline`, `core.Repo`)
- Range: required element (`core.Service`, `core.IntegrationEdge`, `core.Policy`, etc)
"@und .
id:core.rel.is_a rdf:type rocs:Relation .
id:core.rel.is_a rdfs:label "is_a"@und .
id:core.rel.is_a skos:definition "Untertyp/Unterklasse → Obertyp/Oberklasse"@und .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:status "active"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:relationGroup "taxonomy"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:transitive true .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:symmetric false .
id:core.rel.is_a rdf:type owl:TransitiveProperty .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:axisDefault "parents"^^xsd:string .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:example "core.Agent is_a core.Actor"@und .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:antiExample "Using is_a for instances/values (use `instance_of`)"@und .
id:core.rel.is_a rocs:guidanceMarkdown "## Definition
`X is_a Y` means X is a subtype of Y (inherits Y’s meaning/constraints); use for taxonomy only.

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- X is a subtype/specialization of Y (inherits meaning/constraints).

## Do not use when
- You mean instance/value membership (use `instance_of`) or part-whole (use `part_of`).

## Domain / Range
- Domain: subtype concept
- Range: supertype concept
"@und .
